doc.title: Jonathan Scales interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 23, 2025

title: 'The Questions Unanswerable', a college duet
summary: An audio excerpt of his senior-year duet, written to convey wonder about knowledge; Joel Spencer played the top part.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: I think I do. And I’d like to see if you can tell me what you wanted the audience to get or feel out of this.

Oh man. So that’s like a steel pan duet that I wrote when I was a senior in college, called the “The Questions Unanswerable.” And in that piece I was trying to convey this like sense of wonder in like – I was trying to convey this like sense of wonder when it comes to like the acquisition of like knowledge and understanding. Kind of like being in outer space where like the further you go the more you learn. And like seeing outer space where like the further you go the more you learn. And like seeing outer space, it’d be like there’s so much to know, there’s so much to learn. There’s so much out there and we’re curious, like I’m curious of what’s out there and I’m curious of, you know, how does this absorb all the knowledge and stuff that I can and I think that piece was like this college kid about to go into the world and about to step out and see what’s out there. And you know I think I was trying to build a sense of, yeah, just like the mystery of what’s going to the future like? Where is this going? So you know think about it, if that’s my idea going into it, imagine what my note choices are going to be.
It was a duet with another pannist.
Yeah. I was playing the bottom part. I was playing the, like it’s a two-part thing, I was playing the lower voice and my friend Joel Spencer was playing that top steel pan part.
